templates.name: Year in review
templates.line: Four big numbers, a photo strip and a thank-you.
templates.prompt: Create an 8-slide year in review with four key numbers (12 launches, 48 markets, 72K users, 94% retention) and a photo strip.

templates.name: Client proposal
templates.line: Write a client proposal with scope, timeline and three price options
templates.prompt: Write a client proposal as a .docx file. First ask me about the client, the problem to solve, the deliverables, the timeline and my rates; if I have none, use an invented client and label the figures as sample. Structure: a cover, a one-paragraph summary, the scope with what is not included, a timeline table, three price options (essential, standard, premium) in a table, terms and next steps. About 4 pages. Check that the totals add up and that names and dates match throughout, then give me the .docx.

templates.name: Onboarding guide
templates.line: Prepare a 30-day onboarding guide for a new hire
templates.prompt: Write a 30-day onboarding guide as a .docx file. First ask me for the role, the team, the tools they will use and the people they will meet; if I have none, use an invented role and company and label them as sample. Structure: a welcome page, week-by-week goals, a first-day checklist, a who-to-ask table, a glossary and a 30-day check-in with three questions for the manager. Plain, friendly language, about 5 pages, headings and page numbers, then give me the .docx.

templates.name: Lesson plan
templates.line: Write a 45-minute lesson plan with an activity and a quick quiz
templates.prompt: Write a lesson plan as a .docx file. First ask me for the subject, the age or level, the learning objective and the time available; if I have none, use a sample topic and label it as sample. Structure: objectives written as what students will be able to do, materials, a timed sequence (hook, teaching, guided practice, independent task), differentiation for struggling and advanced students, a 5-question exit ticket with answers, and homework. Check that the timings add up to the lesson length. About 2 pages, then give me the .docx.

templates.name: Study guide
templates.line: Turn my course notes into a study guide with practice questions
templates.prompt: Turn my notes into a study guide as a .docx file. First ask me to attach or paste the notes and tell me the exam format. Use only what the notes say, and flag anything missing or unclear instead of filling it in. Structure: a one-page summary, a table of key terms with definitions, the main ideas as short sections, 10 practice questions of mixed difficulty, then an answer key on the last page. Check every answer against the notes, then give me the .docx.

templates.name: Research proposal
templates.line: Draft a research proposal with question, method and timeline
templates.prompt: Draft a research proposal as a .docx file. First ask me for my field, the question I want to answer, the data or participants I could use and my deadline; if I have none, use a sample question and label it as sample. Structure: title, a 150-word abstract, background, research question and hypotheses, method, ethics and risks, a timeline table by month and expected results. Cite nothing you cannot name: mark every reference still to find as [to add]. About 4 pages, then give me the .docx.

templates.name: Literature review
templates.line: Write a literature review using only the sources I give you
templates.prompt: Write a literature review section as a .docx file. First ask me for the topic, the sources (attach them or paste their abstracts) and the citation style. Use only those sources and never invent a reference. Group them by theme rather than one by one, compare their methods and findings, point out agreements and contradictions, and end with the gap my work addresses. Add the reference list in my style and a table of sources by theme. Check every claim against its source, then give me the .docx and a list of anything you could not verify.

templates.name: Investment return calculator
templates.line: Calculate IRR and payback for a project's cash flows
templates.prompt: Build an investment return spreadsheet. First ask me for the upfront cost, the expected cash flow of each year (up to 10) and my discount rate; if I have none, use sample figures and label them as sample. Make one inputs tab and one results tab with live formulas for IRR, NPV, simple and discounted payback, and a chart of cumulative cash flow. Add a scenario cell that scales every cash flow by -20%, 0% or +20%. Cross-check the key results with an independent calculation, tell me what you could not verify, and say in two lines whether the project clears my rate.

templates.name: Cash runway forecast
templates.line: Forecast 12 months of cash with best and worst cases
templates.prompt: Build a 12-month cash forecast. First ask me for the opening balance, monthly revenue, fixed and variable costs and any one-off payments; if I have none, use sample figures and label them as sample. Put the inputs in one tab, with a dropdown that switches between base, best and worst case, and the monthly balance in another, with live formulas. Add a chart of the balance, highlight in red any month below zero, and show how many months of runway remain. Cross-check the key results with an independent calculation, tell me what you could not verify, and summarise the three cases in three lines.

templates.name: Weighted gradebook
templates.line: Track class grades with weighted categories and letter marks
templates.prompt: Build a gradebook for one class. First ask me for the categories and their weights (for example homework, quizzes, exam), the number of assignments and the grade scale; if I have none, use five students with invented names and label them as sample. One row per student, one column per assignment, live formulas for each category average, the weighted final grade and the letter mark from a lookup table. Colour grades below the pass mark, add the class average and a distribution chart. Check that the weights add up to 100%, cross-check the final grades with an independent calculation and tell me what you could not verify.

templates.name: Study-week planner
templates.line: Split my weekly study hours across courses by exam date and difficulty
templates.prompt: Build a study planner spreadsheet. First ask me for my courses, each exam date, how hard I find each one (1 to 5) and how many hours I can study per week; if I have none, use five courses and label them as sample. With formulas, work out how many hours each course gets per week, weighted by difficulty and by how close its exam is, and lay them out on a Monday to Sunday grid. Check that the grid never exceeds my weekly hours, add a countdown in days to each exam and a chart of hours per course, and cross-check the totals independently.

templates.name: Survey results analysis
templates.line: Summarise survey answers with statistics and charts
templates.prompt: Analyse survey results in a spreadsheet. First ask me to attach or paste the responses (CSV or table) and tell me which questions are scales and which are choices; if I have none, create 40 invented responses and label them as sample. Keep the raw data on one tab, untouched. On another tab use formulas for response counts, mean, median and standard deviation per scale question, the share of each choice, and a comparison between two groups I name. Add one chart per question, list the data issues you found (blanks, outliers) and write three plain-language findings. Cross-check the statistics with an independent calculation.

templates.name: Literature matrix
templates.line: Compare the papers I read in one literature matrix
templates.prompt: Build a literature review matrix. First ask me for my research question and the papers to include (titles, DOIs or text I paste); never invent a paper or a figure, and write 'not stated' where a paper does not say. One row per paper: year, method, sample, main finding, limitation and a relevance score from 1 to 5. Add filters, a count per method with formulas, a chart of papers per year and a gap tab listing what none of the papers covers. Check that every row is filled and tell me anything you could not verify.

templates.name: Weekly sales summary
templates.line: Every Monday, summarise last week's sales in one page
templates.prompt: Create an automation that summarises last week's sales every Monday at 8:00. First ask me where the numbers live (a file in my workspace or a connected app), who should get the summary and which figures matter. Steps: read last week's figures, compare them with the week before, write one page with the three biggest changes and a short explanation of each, save it as a file and notify me. Read-only: it never sends, changes or deletes anything. Show me the draft, wait for my yes, save it, then offer to run it once now.

templates.name: Overdue invoice drafts
templates.line: Draft a reminder for every overdue invoice, once a week
templates.prompt: Create an automation that drafts payment reminders every Monday at 9:00. First ask me where my invoices are listed (a file or a connected app), how many days late counts as overdue and the tone I want. Steps: find the overdue invoices, write one polite reminder per client with the amount and the due date, and save them as drafts in one file. It must never send anything: approval stays on 'ask me first'. Show me the draft, wait for my yes, save it, then offer to run it once now.

templates.name: Weekly study plan
templates.line: Every Sunday evening, plan my study week from my deadlines
templates.prompt: Create an automation that plans my study week every Sunday at 18:00. First ask me where my deadlines and exams are listed (a file or my calendar), how many hours I can study each day and which evenings are free. Steps: read the deadlines for the next 14 days, rank what is most urgent, write a day-by-day plan that fits my hours, save it as a file and notify me. Read-only: it never changes my calendar. Show me the draft, wait for my yes, save it, then offer to run it once now.

templates.name: Morning quiz
templates.line: Every weekday morning, quiz me on my notes
templates.prompt: Create an automation that quizzes me every weekday at 7:30. First ask me which folder holds my notes and how many questions I want. Steps: pick the topics I was quizzed on least recently (keep a small log file), write 5 questions of mixed difficulty from my notes only, save the questions and the answers in separate files and notify me with the questions. Never state a fact that is not in my notes. Show me the draft, wait for my yes, save it, then offer to run it once now.

templates.name: New papers digest
templates.line: Every Friday, list new papers on my topic with a two-line summary
templates.prompt: Create an automation that lists new papers on my topic every Friday at 16:00. First ask me for the topic, a few keywords, how far back to look and where to look (for example public preprint servers and journal pages). Steps: search the web, keep only items from the last 7 days, give each a title, link, date and a two-line summary of what its abstract says, mark any you could not open, save the list as a file and notify me. Read-only: it downloads and installs nothing. Show me the draft, wait for my yes, save it, then offer to run it once now.

templates.name: Page change watch
templates.line: Check a web page every day and tell me when it changes
templates.prompt: Create an automation that watches a web page and tells me when it changes. First ask me for the page address, what counts as a change that matters (a new date, a new row, a number) and when to check (by default every day at 9:00). Steps: read the page, compare it with the copy saved last time in a file and, if something that matters changed, write what changed in two lines with the old and new values and notify me. Otherwise stay silent. Read-only. Show me the draft, wait for my yes, save it, then offer to run it once now.

templates.name: Weekly review team
templates.line: A team that prepares my weekly business review
templates.prompt: Create an Agent Team that prepares my weekly business review. First interview me: which numbers matter, where they live (a file or a connected app), who reads the review and what 'done' looks like. Propose the roles, each owning a distinct part (for example a data reader, an analyst, a writer and a checker who verifies every number against its source), with the model for each. Wait for my yes, create the team in my workspace, check that it loads, then tell me how to start a chat with it and suggest a first small job.

templates.name: Customer feedback team
templates.line: A team that turns customer feedback into a ranked fix list
templates.prompt: Create an Agent Team that turns customer feedback into a ranked list of fixes. First interview me: where the feedback comes from (a file or an export), what a good result looks like and who decides. Propose the roles (for example a reader that tags each comment, an analyst that groups themes and counts them, a prioritiser that ranks by impact and effort, a checker that samples comments against the tags), each with its model. Wait for my yes, create it in my workspace, check that it loads, then tell me how to start a chat with it and suggest a first small job on invented comments labelled as sample.

templates.name: Exam tutoring team
templates.line: A team that tutors me for an exam: explain, quiz, verify
templates.prompt: Create an Agent Team that tutors me for an exam. First interview me: the subject, the exam date, what I find hard and how I like to learn. Propose the roles (for example a tutor that explains one idea at a time, a quiz-maker that asks questions from my notes, a checker that verifies every explanation and answer before I see it), each with its model. Wait for my yes, create the team in my workspace, check that it loads, then tell me how to start a chat with it and suggest a first short session.

templates.name: Lesson-prep team
templates.line: A team that prepares my lessons for the week
templates.prompt: Create an Agent Team that prepares my lessons for the week. First interview me: the subject, the level, the curriculum goals and the lessons I teach each day. Propose the roles (for example a planner that sequences the week, a writer that drafts activities and handouts, an assessor that makes the quizzes, a checker that confirms each lesson meets its stated goal), each with its model. Wait for my yes, create it in my workspace, check that it loads, then tell me how to start a chat with it and suggest a first small job.

templates.name: Research and fact-check team
templates.line: A team that answers a research question and checks its sources
templates.prompt: Create an Agent Team that answers a research question and checks its sources. First interview me: the question, the depth I want, which sources count and what 'done' looks like. Propose the roles (for example a scout that finds sources, a reader that extracts the evidence, a fact-checker that confirms each claim against its source, a writer that drafts the answer with links), each with its model. Wait for my yes, create it in my workspace, check that it loads, then tell me how to start a chat with it and suggest a first small question.

templates.name: Peer-review team
templates.line: A team of reviewers that critiques my draft paper before I submit
templates.prompt: Create an Agent Team that reviews my draft paper the way a journal would. First interview me: my field, the target venue and which parts worry me. Propose the roles (for example a methods reviewer, a statistics reviewer, a writing reviewer and an editor who merges the three into one report ranked by severity), each with its model. Wait for my yes, create it in my workspace, check that it loads, then tell me how to start a chat with it. It reports, it never rewrites my text.

templates.name: Meeting minutes skill
templates.line: A skill that turns meeting notes into decisions and owners
templates.prompt: Create a skill called meeting-minutes. First ask me what good minutes look like for my team (sections, length, language). The skill takes pasted notes or a transcript and returns the decisions, the action items (owner, due date) and the open questions as a table, and writes 'owner missing' instead of guessing a name. Write SKILL.md with a clear description and when to use it, test it on an invented meeting, show me the result, then save it in my skills folder.

templates.name: Invoice check skill
templates.line: A skill that checks an invoice against its purchase order
templates.prompt: Create a skill called invoice-check. First ask me which fields matter (supplier, lines, quantities, unit prices, tax rate) and what gap is acceptable. The skill compares an invoice with its purchase order (CSV or pasted lines) using a small script and lists every difference: missing line, wrong price, wrong total, wrong tax. It never approves a payment. Write SKILL.md and the script, test them on two invented documents with one planted error, show me the output, then save it in my skills folder.

templates.name: Rubric marking skill
templates.line: A skill that marks short answers against my rubric
templates.prompt: Create a skill called rubric-marking. First ask me for my rubric (criteria, points, what earns each level) and the question. The skill reads a student's answer and returns, for each criterion, the points and one sentence quoting the answer that justifies them, plus one comment for the student. It flags uncertain cases for me to decide and never gives a final grade alone. Write SKILL.md, test it on three invented answers (strong, average, weak), show me the output, then save it in my skills folder.

templates.name: Vocabulary drill skill
templates.line: A skill that drills a word list with spaced repetition
templates.prompt: Create a skill called vocab-drill. First ask me which language I am learning, my level and where to keep my word list. The skill reads the list, picks the next 10 words with a small script that follows spaced-repetition boxes (a wrong answer comes back tomorrow, a right one in 2, 4, then 8 days), asks them one at a time and saves the results in a JSON file. Write SKILL.md and the script, test two sessions on an invented list of 15 words, show me the file, then save it in my skills folder.

templates.name: Paper card skill
templates.line: A skill that turns a paper into a one-page summary card
templates.prompt: Create a skill called paper-card. First ask me what I want on the card (for example question, method, sample, result, limits, relevance). The skill reads a paper (a PDF or pasted text) and fills the card, quoting a short passage and its page for each result, and writes 'not stated' rather than guessing a number. Write SKILL.md with a clear description and when to use it, test it on a short invented abstract, show me the card, then save it in my skills folder.

templates.name: Citation check skill
templates.line: A skill that finds citations missing from a draft's references
templates.prompt: Create a skill called citation-check. First ask me for my citation style (author-year or numbered). The skill takes a draft and its reference list, matches them with a small script, and lists citations with no reference, references never cited and inconsistent years or spellings. It reports; it never edits my text. Write SKILL.md and the script, test them on an invented draft with three planted errors, show me the report, then save it in my skills folder.
